acceptance_criteria.criterion: ComputeLcs returns the full list as paired indices when both input lists are identical.
ComputeLcs returns an empty list when the two input lists share no common elements.
ComputeLcs correctly identifies the LCS for lists with insertions, deletions, and reorderings (partial overlap).
ComputeLcs performs case-insensitive matching when given StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase.
ClassifyChanges emits Moved entries for same-filename pairs where relative order inverted (reconciliation before replacement detection).
ClassifyChanges emits Replaced entries when a removed mod at reference position R pairs with a new mod at the LCS-aligned current position.
ClassifyChanges classifies remaining new mods as Added (beyond all LCS items) or Inserted (within LCS item range).
ClassifyChanges groups LCS items with differing absolute positions as dependent changes under their causal insertion or deletion.
ClassifyChanges constructs DiffLineModel entries using _localization.GetString() — no hardcoded UI strings.
All 4 new LCS unit tests pass.

summary: Implemented ComputeLcs(IReadOnlyList<string>, IReadOnlyList<string>, StringComparer) as an internal static method in DiffService.cs using a standard DP backtrack approach, returning List<(int refIndex, int curIndex)> in order.

Implemented ClassifyChanges(IReadOnlyList<ModEntryModel>, IReadOnlyList<ModEntryModel>, List<(int,int)>) as an internal static method executing the full 6-step classification pipeline: LCS-shifted detection, same-filename reconciliation (Moved), replacement detection with LCS-aligned position offsets, Added/Inserted classification, and dependent-change grouping under causal insertions/deletions. All DiffLineModel entries are constructed via _localization.GetString() following the existing DiffDialog pattern.
Added InternalsVisibleTo for LoadOrderKeeper.Tests to the main .csproj so tests can call the internal methods directly without reflection.

Added 4 new LCS unit tests: ComputeLcs_ReturnsCorrectLcs_ForIdenticalLists, ComputeLcs_ReturnsCorrectLcs_ForDisjointLists, ComputeLcs_ReturnsCorrectLcs_ForPartialOverlap, ComputeLcs_IsCaseInsensitive. All 4 pass.
All existing DiffServiceTests pass. Total test run: 407 pass / 24 fail — the 24 failures are pre-existing locale/reflection issues unrelated to this WP.

comments.note: DiffService.cs now contains two independent classification systems side by side: the new LCS-based ComputeLcs/ClassifyChanges methods and the legacy DetectReplacements/DetectAndAssignDependentChanges methods. WP-002 will wire in the LCS pipeline; until then, the legacy methods remain in production use. This transient co-existence is by design but the file will need the legacy methods removed once WP-002 lands.

ClassifyChanges uses ReferenceEqualityComparer.Instance for two HashSets tracking ModEntryModel instances. This is correct and intentional (identity comparison to avoid false-positive filename collisions), but is subtle enough that a comment explaining the choice would prevent future confusion.

The InternalsVisibleTo attribute is added via the MSBuild AssemblyAttribute mechanism in the .csproj rather than a dedicated AssemblyInfo.cs. This is the modern idiomatic approach for SDK-style projects, but if the project ever adds an AssemblyInfo.cs, the attribute should be moved there for consistency.

DiffServiceTests.cs previously lacked a 'using System;' directive because implicit usings were not enabled and the only System types used were accessed via System.Linq/Task. Adding StringComparer required adding the directive explicitly — this is correct and follows existing per-file explicit-using conventions in the test project.

summary: Build check: Solution compiles clean — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
Regression: 431 total tests, 407 pass, 24 fail. All 24 failures are pre-existing locale (fr-FR) and reflection issues confirmed in the Developer's handoff notes — none are regressions from this WP.

New LCS tests: All 4 new unit tests (ComputeLcs_ReturnsCorrectLcs_ForIdenticalLists, ComputeLcs_ReturnsCorrectLcs_ForDisjointLists, ComputeLcs_ReturnsCorrectLcs_ForPartialOverlap, ComputeLcs_IsCaseInsensitive) PASS.

AC verification: All 10 acceptance criteria verified. ComputeLcs DP/backtrack logic is correct for identical, disjoint, and partial-overlap inputs. StringComparer is threaded through Equals calls enabling case-insensitivity. ClassifyChanges steps are in correct order (reconciliation before replacement detection, dependent grouping last). All DiffLineModel entries use _localization.GetString() — no hardcoded UI strings. InternalsVisibleTo confirmed in .csproj via MSBuild AssemblyAttribute.

Edge-case analysis: Empty lists return empty LCS cleanly. Null LineNumber falls back to 1-based index in ClassifyChanges. Mods with LineNumber=null are excluded from replacement matching (classified as Added) — correct by contract. Large lists (~1000 mods) allocate ~4MB 2D DP array, acceptable. Duplicate filenames handled conservatively via TryAdd — only first occurrence matched, second remains as unmatched new item.

comments.note: ComputeLcs with empty inputs (one or both lists empty) returns an empty list correctly — the DP loop simply does not execute and the backtrack exits immediately. No defensive null/empty checks needed.

ClassifyChanges: ModEntryModel entries with LineNumber=null fall back to 1-based index in lcsShifted tracking and are excluded from newByCurPos replacement matching (pos==0 guard). These mods will be classified as Added. This is correct per the handoff contract that LineNumber is always populated by FileService.ReadFileAsync before ClassifyChanges is called.

No direct unit test exercises ClassifyChanges in isolation. All classification logic is currently tested through the legacy GetPluginsDiffAsync path. Once WP-002 wires ClassifyChanges into the live pipeline, integration-level test coverage will be provided. Dedicated ClassifyChanges unit tests would be a valuable addition for WP-002 or a follow-on.

comments.note: Added explanatory comment above `reconciledNewMods` HashSet in Step 2: ReferenceEqualityComparer.Instance is intentional because ModEntryModel.Equals() compares by FileName, so the default comparer would incorrectly de-duplicate two distinct instances with the same filename. Identity comparison ensures we track exact objects matched.

Added explanatory comment above `replacements` and `usedForReplacement` in Step 3 with the same ReferenceEqualityComparer.Instance rationale, and separated it visually from the alignment-algorithm comment block for clarity.

Replaced the Step 3 alignment comment block that described two approaches (an abandoned complex one, then 'simpler direct approach') with a single concise description of the actual algorithm: aligned position = R − (count of prior removals), with a one-line explanation of why.

Added inline comment on the `pos > 0` guard in newByCurPos population explaining that pos==0 is a sentinel for LineNumber==null, meaning the entry has no assigned position and cannot participate in replacement matching — it will be classified as Added instead.

ComputeLcs initializes the result list with capacity dp[m,n] — a nice performance micro-optimization that avoids list resizing during backtrack. This pattern is worth preserving in any future variants of the method.

[documentation-forward] ClassifyChanges has no dedicated unit tests — all classification logic is currently validated indirectly through the legacy GetPluginsDiffAsync path. WP-002 is the natural time to add isolated ClassifyChanges tests covering at minimum: Moved (swapped filenames), Replaced, Inserted/Added classification, and dependent-change grouping. The QA coverage-gap comment should be surfaced in the WP-002 spec or test plan.
